feature: Command S saves a video as a project
summary: Command S on a recording now saves your edit as a Photonz project, the choice you made on the card. The first press asks where to put it, later presses save in place, and the recording itself is never written over.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open a screen recording from Capture History.
Park the playhead two seconds in and press Q to trim the start off.
Press Command W. The sheet asks to save, with Export beside Save.
Press Cancel, then Command S, and save the project where the box suggests.
Open another recording, cut it with Command K and drag a second video onto the end of V1.
Press Command S, save, then make one more cut and press Command S again: no box this time.
Close the window and open the .photonz project from Finder.

evaluate: Is a save box on the first Command S what you expect, the way an untitled Premiere project does it?
Should Save be live on a recording you have not touched yet, or dimmed until you change something?
Is Export beside Save on the close sheet useful, or is it one button too many?
Does the project name the window takes after the save read right to you?
rough: The window's title bar still does not show the name, length or saved state the video mocks draw; that is its own task (a-video-window-says-its-name-size-length-and-whe).
The close sheet is four buttons stacked, as macOS draws any alert with four; the mocks draw no close sheet to compare it with.
The walk drives Command S through the same action File > Save runs, because the probe window never comes to the front for the real key chord.
